# Real files

<!-- Generated by `npm run realworld`. Do not edit by hand. -->

biolint is run in its default profile over files that mainstream tools produce and consume: the
[nf-core test datasets](https://github.com/nf-core/test-datasets) at commit `65d3096343da` (402 files of at most 4 MB each;
the list is in `conformance/realworld.json`). No format is forced: each file is detected from its name and content, as a user would run it.

The files were split in two by a hash of their path. Rules were tuned on one half only. The other half was not looked at
until every format was finished, and was then scored once. That first score is frozen in `conformance/holdout-first-run.json`.

## Held-out half, first and only blind run

| Format | Files | No findings | Warnings only | With errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bed | 29 | 25 | 3 | 1 |
| fasta | 58 | 46 | 11 | 1 |
| fastq | 58 | 57 | 0 | 1 |
| gff3 | 8 | 3 | 4 | 1 |
| gtf | 4 | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| sam | 2 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| vcf | 49 | 36 | 11 | 2 |
| **Total** | **208** | **170** | **31** | **7** |

Of the 7 files with errors: 3 genuine-defect, 2 broken-on-purpose, 2 false-positive.

| File | Format | What it was | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ampcombi/general_amps.fasta` | fasta | genuine-defect | A record of this antimicrobial-peptide database dump has the single character `0` in place of a sequence. |
| `genome/genome.gff3` | gff3 | genuine-defect | On 13 lines a score such as `2.48e-03` is split across the score, strand and phase columns (`2`, `48e`, `03`), shifting everything after it. |
| `fastq/test_truncated_halfway.fastq` | fastq | broken-on-purpose | A test fixture cut off inside a record. |
| `vcf/hg002_chr20_90000_to_100000.dnascope.gvcf.gz` | vcf | false-positive | The file has `#FGQB` lines among the records (a vendor extension). biolint 0.1.0-dev mis-reported each as a repeated column header (an error). Fixed: they are now reported once as a comment line among the records (VCF106, a warning). |
| `popgen/plink_simulated.vcf.gz` | vcf | genuine-defect | PLINK's simulated data uses `d` and `D` as alleles. htslib reads the file, but these are not bases, and tools that interpret alleles (for example `bcftools norm`) reject them. |
| `rpbp/reference.annotated.bed.gz` | bed | false-positive | The file has `-1` in thickStart/thickEnd for transcripts without a coding region. biolint reported an error on every such line. Fixed: this convention is now a warning (BED039). |
| `bam/test.paired_end.sorted.invalid.sam` | sam | broken-on-purpose | A test fixture: alignments name reference sequences but the header has no @SQ lines, which samtools refuses. |

A false positive here means biolint reported an error on a file that its producing tool and common readers accept. Both were fixed after the run, so they no longer appear below.

| `popgen/plink_simulated.vcf.gz` | vcf | genuine-defect | PLINK's simulated data uses `d` and `D` as alleles. htslib reads the file, but these are not bases, and tools that interpret alleles (for example `bcftools norm`) reject them. |
| `bam/test.paired_end.sorted.invalid.sam` | sam | broken-on-purpose | A test fixture: alignments name reference sequences but the header has no @SQ lines, which samtools refuses. |

These classifications are the judgement of the biolint authors. SAM has only two files in this collection; the SAM validator was additionally tuned and checked on
several hundred files from the htslib, samtools and pysam test suites and from nf-core BAM files converted with samtools, a run that is not reproduced by this script.
